answer: Mechanism: eccentricity-span routing. Each agent’s transaction neighborhood is scored by eccentricity bands; high-value routes require links spanning from nadir (peripheral low-degree nodes) through mid to summit (central hubs) plus at least one jade cross-community edge. Sybil clusters are locally dense but topologically flat, so they fail the span test. Attacker cost: must sustain diverse real counterparties across unrelated communities, not just duplicate nodes.
